name: Zeus
description: King of the gods, ruler of thunder and sky. Supreme deity of Olympus who wields thunderbolts and maintains order among gods and mortals.

name: Hera
description: Queen of the gods and goddess of marriage, family, and women. Protector of women in childbirth and marriage bonds.

name: Poseidon
description: God of the sea, earthquakes, and horses. Brother of Zeus, controls the waters and wields a trident.

name: Hades
description: God of the underworld and the dead. Brother of Zeus and Poseidon, rules over souls and the realm below.

name: Athena
description: Goddess of wisdom, warfare, and crafts. Daughter of Zeus, born from his head fully armed. Patron of Athens.

name: Apollo
description: God of sun, music, prophecy, and healing. Son of Zeus, archer of divine arrows, and giver of prophecy through oracles.

name: Artemis
description: Goddess of the hunt, wilderness, and the moon. Twin sister of Apollo, known for her virginity and devotion to chastity.

name: Ares
description: God of war, violence, and bloodlust. Son of Zeus and Hera, represents the brutal aspects of warfare.

name: Aphrodite
description: Goddess of love, beauty, and desire. Born from sea foam, she has power over all matters of love and attraction.

name: Hermes
description: Messenger of the gods and god of thieves, commerce, and travelers. Son of Zeus, known for his cunning and swiftness.

name: Demeter
description: Goddess of agriculture, grain, and the harvest. Sister of Zeus, mother of Persephone, connected to cycles of growth and death.

name: Hestia
description: Goddess of the hearth, home, and family. Eldest Olympian, quiet and serene, worshipped in every household.

name: Hephaestus
description: God of blacksmiths, fire, and craftsmanship. Lame from birth, he creates divine weapons and tools in his forge.

name: Dionysus
description: God of wine, theater, ecstasy, and revelry. Twice-born, represents transformation and the wild aspects of nature.

name: Kronos
description: Titan and father of Zeus. Ruled during the Golden Age before being overthrown by his son.

name: Rhea
description: Titaness and mother of the Olympian gods. Helped protect infant Zeus from Kronos.

name: Persephone
description: Daughter of Demeter, abducted by Hades and became queen of the underworld. Represents spring's return and winter's darkness.

name: Hecate
description: Goddess of magic, crossroads, and boundaries. Associated with witchcraft and nocturnal wanderings.

name: Nike
description: Goddess of victory and success. Usually depicted as winged, accompanying warriors into battle.

name: Prometheus
description: Titan who gave fire to humanity and was punished by Zeus with eternal torment. Symbol of defiance and sacrifice.

name: Pan
description: God of shepherds, flocks, and wild nature. Half-human, half-goat, known for his pipes and chaotic energy.

name: Iris
description: Goddess of the rainbow, servant of Hera and messenger of the gods. Personifies the rainbow itself.

name: Nemesis
description: Goddess of retribution and divine vengeance. Punishes hubris and imbalance, restoring justice.

name: Ouranos
description: Primordial sky god, father of the Titans. Castrated by Kronos and succeeded him.

name: Gaia
description: Primordial earth goddess, mother of all. Represents the living earth and fertility.

name: Leto
description: Titaness and mother of Apollo and Artemis. Pursued by Hera's jealousy for bearing Zeus's children.

name: Maia
description: Pleiad and mother of Hermes. One of the seven sisters who form the constellation Pleiades.

name: Heracles
description: Greatest hero of Greek mythology, son of Zeus and mortal woman Alcmene. Known for his twelve labors and immense strength.

name: Perseus
description: Heroic demigod, son of Zeus and Danaë. Famous for slaying Medusa with her own severed head.

name: Achilles
description: Greatest warrior of the Trojan War, son of Thetis and Peleus. Nearly invulnerable except for his heel.

name: Hector
description: Prince of Troy and greatest Trojan warrior. Son of Priam and Hecuba, killed by Achilles in the Trojan War.

name: Odysseus
description: King of Ithaca, known for his intelligence and cunning. Led the Trojan Horse scheme and faced trials returning home.

name: Helen
description: Most beautiful woman in the world, daughter of Zeus and Leda. Her abduction by Paris sparked the Trojan War.

name: Medusa
description: Gorgon monster with snakes for hair whose gaze turns people to stone. Slain by Perseus who used her head as a weapon.

name: Cerberus
description: Three-headed guard dog of the underworld, child of Typhon and Echidna. Guards the gates of Hades.

name: Minotaur
description: Creature with human body and bull's head, child of Pasiphae. Imprisoned in the Labyrinth of Crete.

name: Chimera
description: Hybrid monster with lion front, goat middle, and serpent tail. Breathes fire and was slain by Bellerophon.

name: Hydra
description: Serpent with multiple heads that regenerate when cut off. One of the Twelve Labors of Heracles.

name: Jason
description: Prince of Thessaly and leader of the Argonauts. Sailed the ship Argo in quest of the Golden Fleece.

name: Theseus
description: King of Athens and great hero. Slew the Minotaur, unified Attica, and performed many great deeds.

name: Paris
description: Prince of Troy who abducted Helen, sparking the Trojan War. Son of Priam and Hecuba.

name: Menelaus
description: King of Sparta and husband of Helen. Fought in the Trojan War to recover his wife.

name: Agamemnon
description: King of Mycenae and commander of the Greek forces in the Trojan War. Killed by his wife Clytemnestra.

name: Patroclus
description: Companion and closest friend of Achilles in the Trojan War. Killed by Hector, his death motivated Achilles's return.

name: Danaë
description: Princess of Argos, mother of Perseus. Imprisoned in bronze tower but Zeus reached her as golden rain.

name: Alcmene
description: Princess of Mycenae and mortal mother of Heracles. Wife of Amphitryon, seduced by Zeus.

name: Priam
description: King of Troy during the Trojan War. Father of many children including Hector and Paris.

name: Hecuba
description: Queen of Troy and wife of Priam. Mother of Hector, Paris, and many others. Survived the fall of Troy.

name: Leda
description: Queen of Sparta, mother of Helen and Clytemnestra. Seduced by Zeus in form of a swan.

name: Peleus
description: King of the Myrmidons and father of Achilles. Married the sea nymph Thetis.

name: Thetis
description: Sea nymph and mother of Achilles. Tried to make her son immortal by dipping him in the River Styx.

name: Aegeus
description: King of Athens and father of Theseus. Threw himself into the sea (Aegean Sea) after thinking his son was dead.

name: Troy
description: Ancient city in Asia Minor, setting of the Trojan War. Besieged for 10 years by Greek forces.

name: Mount Olympus
description: Mountain in Greece where the Olympian gods dwell. Highest peak in Greece with divine palaces above the clouds.

name: Underworld
description: Realm below the earth ruled by Hades. Where souls of the dead reside after death. Contains Tartarus and Elysium.

name: Tartarus
description: Deepest part of the underworld where defeated Titans are imprisoned. Surrounded by bronze walls.

name: Elysium
description: Blessed realm in the underworld where virtuous souls dwell in peace and happiness after death.

name: Sparta
description: City-state in Greece, home of Helen and Menelaus. Known for warriors and military culture.

name: Athens
description: Major city-state in Greece, patron goddess Athena. Home of many famous heroes including Theseus.

name: Labyrinth
description: Intricate maze on Crete built by Daedalus. Contained the Minotaur and was inescapable.

name: Delphi
description: Sacred site and sanctuary of Apollo in Greece. Home to the Oracle of Delphi who gave prophecies.

name: Crete
description: Island in the Mediterranean, home of King Minos and the Minotaur. Significant in Greek mythology.

name: Colchis
description: Kingdom at the edge of the world where Jason sought the Golden Fleece. Home of Medea.

name: Penelope
description: Queen of Ithaca and wife of Odysseus. Waited faithfully for her husband's return for ten years, fending off persistent suitors.

name: Telemachus
description: Son of Odysseus and Penelope. Grew to manhood while his father was lost, learning to be a prince and eventually helping his father.

name: Hebe
description: Goddess of youth and spring, cupbearer of the gods. Daughter of Zeus and Hera.

name: Triton
description: Sea god and messenger of the sea, son of Poseidon and Amphitrite. Half-human, half-fish, carries a conch trumpet.

name: Polyphemus
description: Giant Cyclops with a single eye in his forehead. Son of Poseidon, blinded by Odysseus and his men in the cave.

name: Eros
description: God of love and desire. Son of Aphrodite, usually depicted as a winged boy with arrows that cause love.

name: Aeneas
description: Trojan hero, son of Aphrodite and the mortal Anchises. Survived Troy's fall and sailed to found Rome.
